1.explanation:
1. Search/Search.js: contains the React/web component logic that renders the search field, the clear icon button, and the autofill hook.
2. Search/_search.scss: styles the clear icon (color, hover, focus) in the Search component under normal backgrounds.
3. TextInput/TextInput.js: underlying input wrapper used by Search; defines how browser autofill is applied.
4. TextInput/_text-input.scss: includes the WebKit autofill overrides (–webkit-text-fill-color, background-clip) that trigger the sky-blue fill in Chrome.
5. ToolbarSearch/ToolbarSearch.js and its _toolbar-search.scss: a variant of Search used in toolbars that also needs autofill and clear-icon styles; inspecting it provides guidance for consistent autofill fixes across components.

Together, these files control how the Search input and its clear icon are rendered and styled both normally and under Chrome’s autofill. Modifying the clear-icon color or autofill overrides here will reproduce and fix the color-contrast issue.
1.bug_scenario: In Chrome, when the search input is autofilled (sky-blue background) the clear (“×”) icon button in the Search component does not meet contrast requirements against that background. The screenshot shows the Search input with the user’s autofilled text highlighted in bright sky-blue, the “×” clear icon inside the input, and the Submit button to the right. Because we only style the clear icon for the default input background, it becomes too light against Chrome’s autofill blue. To reproduce, focus the Search input in Chrome, let it autofill, and observe the clear icon on its blue fill.
